surge.method: Linear wave theory on the nearest buoy's swell and wind waves; peak near-bottom water speed. Fine sand starts moving at about 0.15 m/s (0.5 ft/s).

season.text: Open Oct 2, 2026 (6 p.m.) to Mar 17, 2027. 7 per person, 3 1/4 in carapace, divers by hand only, report card required.

season.label: Rockfish and lingcod (Southern Management Area)
season.text: Boat-based anglers: nearshore rockfish, cabezon and greenlings closed; shelf rockfish and lingcod seaward of 50 fathoms only. Divers and shore anglers are exempt from these season and depth limits.

divers.freedive: Solo freediving is outside our thresholds in any conditions: one up, one down. Never hyperventilate. Size exposure protection for the bottom temperature, not the surface.

suit.text: Suit: 3-5 mm for most divers, sized for 74°F at 60 ft in the nearest glider profile. Kelp-bed bottoms can run colder when internal tides push cold water in.

best_bet.text: Best bet from shore: La Jolla Shores (marginal, with sets around 1 ft at the entry in the CDIP model).

hunting_vis.text: Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 10-15ft at Coronado Islands on Nov 9: enough to hunt pelagics (15 ft or more).

not_covered: Fish counts. No licensed source yet, so the fishing view shows where the water matches each species, not how many fish are there.
Bait at barges other than Everingham's three (Oceanside, Newport, San Pedro, Redondo, Marina del Rey): they post by phone or social media, so only reports from the water cover them.
Current at dive depth. HF radar measures the surface only and is blank within about 1.5 miles of shore.
Beach water-quality notices. San Diego County's beach status site has no public data feed; connecting it needs a feed from the county.
The thermocline at the kelp. The observed profile comes from a glider offshore; the SCCOOS Del Mar kelp mooring did not answer when this was built.
Boats without AIS (most under 65 ft), and Mexican waters beyond shore-receiver range.

species.label: Bluefin tuna
species.note: Sport-fleet catch peaks at 63-70°F (Runcie 2019); in warmer surface water bluefin go deep, out of reach of surface gear.

species.label: Yellowfin tuna
species.note: Holds on the warm, clear side of fronts (Block 1997); a shallow mixed layer pushes it up.

species.label: Dorado (mahi)
species.note: The paddy fish: 75% of Mexican Pacific catch at chlorophyll 0.05-0.25 mg/m³ (Marín-Enríquez 2018).

species.label: Yellowtail (offshore, paddy fish)
species.note: San Diego catch rates rise at 64-68°F and fall above 69°F (Squire 1982; inshore fleet data).

species.label: Striped marlin
species.note: San Diego catch averaged 67.8°F; works breaks and blue water against green over the banks.

species.label: Wahoo
species.note: A warm-year visitor (CPFV: 42 in 2014, 256 in 2015); holds on banks and high spots.

fleet_recent.coverage_note: AIS is heard only within roughly 30-50 nm of shore receivers, and most boats under 65 ft never broadcast it.

inshore.label: Yellowtail (islands and kelp)
inshore.drivers: Warm-year regime (landings swing from under 10,000 to 450,000 fish), bait: squid, sardine, mackerel.
inshore.look: Outer kelp edge next to deep water, up-current points at the islands.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the regime; the 64-66°F 'switch' is angler lore.
inshore.today: Surface water is 76°F; San Diego catch rates have fallen above 69°F in fleet data.

inshore.label: White seabass
inshore.drivers: Spawning Mar-Jul (peak May); tagged fish spent half their time at 55-61°F, tracking the thermocline.
inshore.look: Kelp near squid grounds, at dusk; near the surface Apr-Oct, deeper Dec-Feb.
inshore.evidence: Thermal niche from one tagging study (Aalbers & Sepulveda 2015).
inshore.today: Surface water is 76°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 220 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it.

inshore.label: Calico (kelp) bass
inshore.drivers: Small home ranges; spawns Jun-Aug at 25-60 ft under kelp.

inshore.label: Market squid (the bait that drives the inshore bite)
inshore.drivers: Landings crash after big El Niños; eggs at 50-58°F.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the El Niño effect: a weak squid year is likely this winter.

fishing.method: Profiles say where the water matches what each species needs, not how many fish are there. Water temperature is the satellite map's; breaks are the strongest gradient within 10 nm of a spot, read as the temperature change across 4.3 nm. A cue met at most in-range spots that day is 'everywhere' and singles nothing out.
fishing.counts_note: No dock counts: the network that publishes SoCal landing counts now forbids automated collection and republishing without a license.

bottom_line: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove and Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs; marginal at La Jolla Shores and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 4 to 7 feet from 280°, with a high rip current risk.
By boat today: outside our thresholds for the Coronados; marginal for the offshore banks, Catalina and the San Pedro Channel, and the outer islands; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore.
Nearshore buoys read 75-76°F as of 5:26 PM; the latest satellite temperature map is from Nov 8.

fishing: By boat today: outside our thresholds for the Coronados; marginal for the offshore banks, Catalina and the San Pedro Channel, and the outer islands; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore.
Water at the named spots runs 69-75°F on the Nov 8 satellite map; the strongest break is near San Salvador Knoll, 1.8°F over 4.3 nm, warm side to the E.
Season and water both match today for bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna, dorado, yellowtail, striped marlin and wahoo. That says the water is right, not that fish are there.
AIS shows 4 boats at sea in the last 3 hours, 2 of them stopped. Over the last three days the fleet stopped longest at 33.59N 118.16W.
diving: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove and Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs; marginal at La Jolla Shores and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 4 to 7 feet from 280°, with a high rip current risk.
Best bet from shore: La Jolla Shores (marginal, with sets around 1 ft at the entry in the CDIP model). Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 10-15ft at Coronado Islands on Nov 9.

Suit: 3-5 mm for most divers, sized for 74°F at 60 ft in the nearest glider profile. Kelp-bed bottoms can run colder when internal tides push cold water in. A glider 11 nm from San Diego measured 74°F at the surface and 74°F at 100 ft, with the sharpest drop near 220 ft (8:02 AM Nov 10).
spearfishing: Entries today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove and Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs; marginal at La Jolla Shores and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 4 to 7 feet from 280°, with a high rip current risk.
Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 10-15ft at Coronado Islands on Nov 9: enough to hunt pelagics (15 ft or more).

A glider 11 nm from San Diego measured 74°F at the surface and 74°F at 100 ft, with the sharpest drop near 220 ft (8:02 AM Nov 10). White seabass: Surface water is 76°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 220 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it. Open now: spiny lobster (by hand only).

fishing: Since Nov 2, water warmed in 4 zones and cooled in 3; the biggest move was San Clemente Is. (+2.2°F). Warmest: Rockpile / Upper 500 at 75.0°F; coolest: Tanner / Cortes at 69.2°F.
Strongest offshore break: Tanner / Cortes, 1.2°F over 4.3 nm at 32 52 x 119 32, warm side E. It has held steady over the last three map days.
The paddy drift model's core regions sit in Tanner / Cortes.

AIS-tracked boats stopped longest in 14 Mile / Avalon Bank over the last three days (1.9 h). The same weeks last year, the fleet's stops concentrated at Tanner / Cortes (150 h), 14 Mile / Avalon Bank (41 h) and Catalina (16 h).
Our model's windiest daytime spot in the next days: South 9 / 302 / 425, WNW 13 kt on Tue.
El Niño: weekly Niño-3.4 anomaly +3.3°C, from +3.2°C four weeks earlier.
diving: Predicted visibility today: La Jolla Cove about 14 ft (8-24); La Jolla Shores about 14 ft (8-24); Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs about 9 ft (5-16); Laguna Beach about 10 ft (6-15). Our model's number, scaled to where recent shop reports landed: La Jolla x0.55 from 45 reports; Laguna Beach x0.30 from 18 reports.
Just Get Wet (La Jolla) visibility posts: 10-15 ft on Nov 9, against 10-15 ft on Nov 1.
Water at the La Jolla nearshore buoy: 75.6°F, -0.1°F over a week and +1.7°F since Sep 28.
Set height at the entries (CDIP model): La Jolla Cove Tue 4 ft, Wed 3 ft, Thu 3 ft; La Jolla Shores Tue 1 ft, Wed 1 ft, Thu under 1 ft; Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs Tue 5 ft, Wed 4 ft, Thu 4 ft.
Offshore water column (Spray gliders, nearest each day): the warm top layer reached 187 ft on Nov 10, against 213 ft on Nov 5; 74.2°F at 60 ft.
White seabass: Surface water is 76°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 220 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it.
Yellowtail (islands and kelp): Surface water is 76°F; San Diego catch rates have fallen above 69°F in fleet data.
